title: Rebasing Safely
description: Practice rebasing safely through a concrete team scenario.

blocks.content: **Rebasing** is a way to move or combine commits. Instead of merging two branches (which creates a merge commit), rebasing replays your commits one by one on top of another branch. The result is a cleaner, linear history.

## How Rebase Works

Suppose your `feature` branch is behind `main` because teammates have made new commits:

```
main:    A - B - C - D
feature: A - B - E - F
```

After `git rebase main` on the feature branch:

```
main:    A - B - C - D
feature: A - B - C - D - E' - F'
```

Your commits E and F are replayed on top of D. The history looks like you started from the latest version of main. (The `'` marks mean the commits have new IDs.)

## Running a Rebase

```
git switch feature/my-thing
git rebase main
```

If there are conflicts during rebase, Git stops at each problematic commit. Resolve the conflict, then:
```
git add filename
git rebase --continue
```

To abandon a rebase in progress:
```
git rebase --abort
```

## The Golden Rule of Rebasing

> **Never rebase commits that have already been pushed and shared with others.**

Rebase rewrites commit IDs. If your teammates already have your old commits, rewriting them causes serious confusion. Only rebase local commits that haven't been pushed yet.

Rebasing moves your branch so it appears to start from a newer commit. It can make a story neat, but it rewrites the labels on commits.

Treat shared commits like a group document: do not quietly rewrite them. Rebase your own local work, and communicate before changing shared history.

blocks.question: When is it unsafe to rebase a branch?
options: When the branch has more than 10 commits
When other people have already pulled or based work on those commits
When the branch is more than a week old
When you're not on the main branch
blocks.explanation: Rebasing rewrites commit history - the same changes get new commit IDs. If your teammates already have the original commits, the rewritten history will conflict with theirs and cause confusion. Only rebase commits that exist only on your local machine and haven't been shared.
